severity_policy.blocking: The PR should not merge because the changed behavior is broken, unsafe, or violates a hard architecture boundary.
severity_policy.high: A likely production or data-loss regression, security/privacy issue, or serious cross-platform contract risk.
severity_policy.medium: A concrete bug, edge case, maintainability trap, or missing proof tied directly to changed behavior.
severity_policy.low: A small but actionable correctness, proof, or maintainability risk tied to changed behavior.
severity_policy.nitpick: Optional changed-line polish with no behavior risk, such as readability, naming, tiny duplication, stale comments, dead code, type clarity, or local consistency.

nitpick_policy.risk: No behavior-risk requirement; use for optional polish only.

control_warn_types.Proof Gap: Important changed behavior lacks focused proof.
control_warn_types.Review Limitation: Bunny lacked full packet/context to prove a suspected issue.
control_warn_types.CI Timing: Expected checks were missing, pending, or not yet observable when posted.
control_warn_types.Non-blocking Coverage: Useful coverage or context note that should not block merge by itself.

path_instructions.name: Architecture, KISS, YAGNI, and SOLID
checks: Keep dependency direction from platform apps toward shared core; core must not import app internals or concrete native APIs.
Preserve a single authoritative owner for persisted state; flag divergent writable copies and stale async writes.
Prefer the smallest implementation satisfying current requirements; flag speculative configuration, registries, wrappers, and dependencies only with a concrete cost.
Apply SOLID through existing responsibilities, provider seams, substitutable adapter contracts, focused capabilities, and platform-service boundaries; do not require classes or DI frameworks.
Do not demand abstractions solely to remove similar-looking code, arbitrary size limits, or broad rewrites of untouched code.
A quality finding must explain the changed-line problem and smallest useful fix; put optional polish in nitpicks and uncertain design concerns in open questions.

path_instructions.name: Shared core and platform adapters
checks: Core business logic uses IPlatformService instead of direct Tauri/Expo APIs; inspect all affected adapter implementations when changing the interface.
Core contains shared hooks and Zustand stores; do not impose a React-free rule copied from another repository.
Preserve native transport abort/dispose behavior, data-root selection, and platform-specific error contracts.

path_instructions.name: Reader, import, persistence, and sync
checks: Preserve EPUB/PDF locations, chapter boundaries, annotations, reading progress, and statistics across reopen and pagination.
Check import eligibility, deduplication, file/database consistency, partial failures, and migration compatibility.
Sync must preserve tombstones and conflict resolution; failed transfers must not report success or discard local data.
Book resources and WebView messages are untrusted input; validate paths, payloads, and session identity at boundaries.

path_instructions.name: AI, translation, and audio
checks: Check streaming cancellation, provider configuration, source attribution, and content/credential privacy.
Audio playback cursor, queue, pause/resume, and callbacks must stay associated with the current book and session.
Native lifecycle and dependency patches must preserve background playback and resource cleanup.

path_instructions.name: Desktop native boundary
checks: Check command inputs, filesystem scope, capabilities, persistent data paths, and desktop update behavior.
Keep shared platform contracts consistent with Rust command results and cancellation/error semantics.

path_instructions.name: Shlai builds, identities, and updates
checks: Keep upstream, dev, preview, and stable app identities and storage separate.
PR APK builds stay secret-free; stable signing remains in the minimal shlai-production job after an unsigned build.
Preserve canonical version/tag validation, monotonically increasing versionCode, signer verification, and channel-specific update assets.
Pin workflow actions to reviewed commit SHAs. Privileged Bunny tooling comes from main and inspects PR files as data without executing them.
Bunny is advisory and does not replace Validate, Preview APK, owner approval, or workflow approval for fork builds.

path_instructions.name: Documentation and upstream synchronization
checks: Keep Shlai behavior and release instructions distinct from official ReadAny.
Upstream synchronization preserves branding, package identity, signing boundaries, attribution, and the reviewable PR process.
